chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yasin al-Darir, from Hariz, from the one who informed him, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

I asked him: From where is it befitting to take the pebbles of the Jamarah? He said: Do not take them from two places: from outside the Haram, and from the pebbles of the Jamarah; and there is no problem with taking them from the rest of the Haram.
ai.seo_question: Where should one take the pebbles for stoning the Jamarat during Hajj?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the ritual purity and validity of the pebbles used in the stoning of the Jamarat by distinguishing between the sacred precincts (Haram) and the specific pile itself. It establishes that while pebbles must not be taken from outside the Haram or from the designated 'Jamarah' pile, they may be collected from any other part of the Haram, reflecting the Shia emphasis on the sanctity of the location over the material itself. This ruling underscores the theological view that the act of stoning is a symbolic ritual performed with any valid pebble, provided it originates from the holy boundary.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Muhammad Bin Ahmad, from Muhammad Bin Isa, from Yaseen Al Zareyr, from Hareyz, from the one who informed him, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, said, ‘

I asked himasws, ‘From where is it befitting to take the pebbles (for pelting) the Jamarah?’ Heasws said: ‘Do not take it from two places – from outside the Harram, and from the pebbles of Al-Jamarah; and there is no problem with taking it from the rest of the Al-Harram’.
en.sarwar: 9. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Muhammad ibn ‘Isa from Yasin al-Darir from Hariz from those who narrated to him who has said the following:

“I once asked abu ‘ Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, ‘From where the pebbles must be taken?’ He (the Imam) said, ‘You must not take them from two places, from non-al-Haram (the sacred area) and from the pebble of al-Jamar. It is not harmful to take them from other parts of al-Haram (the sacred area).”’
